newsitem.title: FINLAND: RAUMA SAYS UPM TO CUT STAKE IN IT.
newsitem.headline: RAUMA SAYS UPM TO CUT STAKE IN IT.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Rauma Oy said in a statement on Tuesday that its biggest owner, forestry group UPM-Kymmene Oy, would launch an offering of Rauma shares, cutting its stake to around 35 percent from 60 percent.
The offering to international and domestic investors would comprise 10.5 million shares, a greenshoe option of a further 1.6 million shares and a retail offering of 300,000 shares, Rauma said.
In addition, UPM-Kymmene would offer one million shares to Rauma for redemption.
"As a result of the offering, assuming the greenshoe is exercised, and the buy back, UPM-Kymmene's stake in Rauma will be reduced further to a level of around 35 percent," it said.
UPM earlier cut its stake to 59.9 percent from 73.3 percent by paying part of its 1996 dividend in Rauma shares.
The reduction of its stake reflected "UPM-Kymmene's longer term objective to retan a significant but minority shareholding in Rauma," UPM-Kymmene said in a separate statement.

"Both UPM-Kymmene and Rauma have agreed that they will not, after the proposed transaction, issue or sell further shares in the company for a period until the end of 1998 and the end of 1997 respectively, without the prior consent of the global co-ordinator," UPM said.
SBC Warburg is the global co-ordinator. The international offering would be structured as a single global tranche. The pricing was expected to take place late in May.
